clue.text: Augustus who painted smallest room

definitions.meaning: Augustus ... was a Welsh portrait painter of the early twentieth century
the smallest room is a euphemism for the lavatory

explanation.surface: A question about which painter named Augustus decorated the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the painter's surname, and a slang word for a toilet, which British euphemism calls the smallest room.

clue.text: High taxation in East Yorkshire city? Not quite

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: in says the tax goes inside the shortened city name
not quite means the city's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire
VAT, value added tax, is the British sales tax

explanation.surface: A grumble that a Yorkshire city charges heavy taxes, with a doubt about its exact location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Yorkshire city' looks like one place, such as Hull, but East gives only E; the city is in West Yorkshire. 'Not quite' drops its last letter and 'in' sets the tax inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something high is raised up, or elevated, above its surroundings.

clue.text: Pole not entirely free

indicators.note: not entirely means the synonym is used short of its final letter

parts.note: spare can mean free, as in spare time

explanation.surface: A Polish man who is not completely at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a nationality; it is the long pole, such as a ship's mast or boom.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a spar is a stout pole, used especially as a mast or boom on a ship.

clue.text: Old people dancing, for instance

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about, so instance is rearranged

explanation.surface: Elderly folk, for example the ones taking to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link; the anagram is of INSTANCE alone, dancing being its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancients are people of long ago, so the plural noun fits old people.

clue.text: Girl and boy with ducks

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
Des, short for Desmond, is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl and a boy out with some ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' looks like the birds; it is the verb, as in ducks a question.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym verb: someone who ducks a question or a blow avoids it, that is, evades it.

clue.text: Running up Mark 1 — French Connection garment of the old school

indicators.note: in a down clue running up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a note is a mark, as in take note
1 points to the solution of 1 down, and Jack is a familiar form of that first name
et is the French word for and, a connecting word

explanation.surface: A garment from the French Connection fashion chain's Mark 1 range, worn at an old-fashioned school.
explanation.walkthrough: French Connection looks like the clothing brand; it means the French connecting word ET. The 1 is a cross-reference to 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A short black jacket formerly worn by younger boys at Eton College, so literally a garment of an old school.

clue.text: Come to pass, possibly, in northern England

definitions.meaning: to come to pass is to occur or take place
in northern English dialect the same word is used to mean perhaps or maybe

explanation.surface: Something that may well occur up in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the standard verb meaning occur, and the northern English dialect adverb meaning perhaps.

clue.text: Take off old prime minister

definitions.meaning: to take off the skin of fruit is to ... it
Sir Robert ... was British prime minister in the 1830s and 1840s and founded the police

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove a former head of government from office.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the verb meaning strip off a skin, and the surname of Sir Robert Peel, a nineteenth-century British prime minister.

clue.text: Men left work on deck

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers
op, short for opus, is a work of music

explanation.surface: Sailors abandoned their jobs while on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word here. Orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is a ship's lowest deck, so the answer is an example of a deck.

clue.text: Probationary period in order to turn on pervert?

indicators.note: turn says the little word on is turned round

parts.note: to vitiate is to corrupt or spoil, to pervert

explanation.surface: A trial period designed to arouse a deviant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order to' is a link phrase; 'turn on' looks like the arousing idiom, but 'turn' just turns the little word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A novitiate is the trial period a novice spends before taking religious vows.

clue.text: Don't worry about room occupied by obnoxious people

indicators.note: occupied by says the room has the unpleasant people inside it
about says the word for room is turned back to front

parts.note: a den is a small private room
vermin is a contemptuous name for nasty, worthless people

explanation.surface: Advice not to fret about a room full of horrible people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like part of the phrase 'worry about' but reverses DEN to NED, which holds VERMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase is said to tell someone not to bother or not to worry about something.

clue.text: Quarters found by comrade somewhere in the Himalayas

parts.note: N and E are two compass quarters, north and east
a pal is a friend or comrade

explanation.surface: Lodgings discovered by a friend in the Himalayas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' looks like lodgings; it means points of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the country lies across the Himalayas between India and China.

clue.text: Bottom or top in US assembly

indicators.note: assembly means the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A question of who comes out at the bottom or the top in an American legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link. 'Bottom' looks like the opposite of 'top' in the surface; it is the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorous slang: the part of the body one sits on is the bottom, or buttocks.

clue.text: Horse finding way over river

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales

explanation.surface: A horse discovering a path across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a steed is a horse, especially a spirited riding horse.

clue.text: Dogmatic traveller rising or appearing in hollow

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller

indicators.note: appearing in says the little word sits inside the word for hollow

parts.note: something hollow is empty

explanation.surface: A dogmatic salesman going up, or turning up in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' looks like a valley noun; it is the adjective, and 'appearing in' sets the little word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: peremptory means insisting on immediate obedience, allowing no discussion, much like dogmatic.

clue.text: Tin cans made of tin

indicators.note: made says these letters are made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that tin cans are, unsurprisingly, made of tin.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a tautology; the definition is just 'of tin', with 'made' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stannic is the chemical adjective for tin, from Latin stannum, meaning relating to tin.

clue.text: One article from China for lover of Wuthering Heights

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so the article is removed

parts.note: Cathay is an old poetic name for China
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A single item from China for a fan of the Brontë novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lover of Wuthering Heights' sounds like a reader who loves the book; it is the heroine loved by Heathcliff.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathy Earnshaw is Heathcliff's beloved in Emily Brontë's novel Wuthering Heights.

clue.text: Bush may be a sort of statesman

definitions.meaning: a shrub with white flowers and dark berries
an ... statesman is a respected senior figure

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the American president Bush could be called a statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the US president; it is the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a shrub of the genus Sambucus, and the word before statesman in the phrase elder statesman.

clue.text: Established group

definitions.meaning: something ... is fixed or established, as in ... in its ways
a group of things or people that belong together

explanation.surface: A group that has been around for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the adjective meaning fixed or settled, and the noun meaning a collection.

clue.text: Rusty one revised for medieval contests

indicators.note: revised says these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone out of practice getting a refresher for jousting events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word between the anagram and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourneys were medieval tournaments, mock combats between knights.

clue.text: Car turned up on time, but it's not working

parts.note: the Ka is a small car made by Ford

indicators.note: turned says the little word up is turned round

explanation.surface: The car arrived punctually, but it has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up on time' reads as punctual arrival; it is KA, UP turned to PU, and T. 'but it's' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput, from German, means broken or no longer functioning.

clue.text: Breakfast food that's served in jug

definitions.meaning: oatmeal boiled in milk or water is eaten at breakfast
jug is slang for prison, and ... is British slang for a prison sentence, served or done

explanation.surface: A breakfast dish poured from a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' looks like a pitcher; it is prison, and a sentence is 'served'. The British TV sitcom Porridge was set in a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: oat breakfast, and British slang for time spent in prison, which one serves in jug.

clue.text: Forceful policemen holding a crowd back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembly is read backwards
holding says the police abbreviation is wrapped round the crowd

parts.note: CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is the British plain-clothes police
a crowd is many people

explanation.surface: Police forcing a crowd to retreat with heavy-handed tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts the crowd inside the police letters, and 'back' then turns the whole run round, giving CIMANYD read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dynamic means energetic and forceful.

clue.text: Flipping Scotsman notices water nymphs

indicators.note: flipping says the name is flipped over, read backwards

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name
ads, advertisements, are notices

explanation.surface: A furious Scot spots some water nymphs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild oath; it reverses IAN to NAI.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth naiads are nymphs living in rivers, springs and lakes.

clue.text: Persian, possibly, with paperback King James Bible in stock?

indicators.note: in says the Bible letters go inside the animal

parts.note: a Persian is a breed of cat
the back of the word paper is its final letter
AV, the Authorised Version, is the King James Bible

explanation.surface: A Persian kept with a cheap edition of the Bible on the shop shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks like goods held by a shop; it is the old neckcloth. 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock is a wide band of cloth worn round the neck, much like a cravat.

clue.text: Quite articulate? Lucy is heartless

parts.note: to utter is to articulate, to say aloud

indicators.note: heartless means the name loses its middle, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A question whether a cruel Lucy is well spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. 'articulate' looks like an adjective, well spoken; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: utterly and quite both mean completely, as in quite mad.

clue.text: Order cited in order

indicators.note: in order here means put into a fresh order, rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction quoted in its proper sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' and 'in order' play on two senses: a command, and a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an edict is an official order or decree.

clue.text: Novel about a male: Orlando?

indicators.note: about says the whole run is turned round

parts.note: Orlando is the setter of this puzzle, so the name means me

explanation.surface: The setter asks whether a novel about a man is his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning'; it reverses A, M and ME together.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen.

clue.text: Girl on location for studios, making things tougher

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
Ealing in west London is home to the famous Ealing film studios

explanation.surface: A girl on a film set makes life harder for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is only a link word, the girl's name coming first; Ealing Studios in London made the classic Ealing comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealing heats and slowly cools metal or glass to toughen it, so it makes materials tougher.

clue.text: Seaweed included in botanical garden

indicators.note: included in says the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A seaweed among the plants of a botanic garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: seaweeds are large marine algae, so a single one is an alga.

clue.text: Good booze responsible for a lot of wind?

parts.note: ale is beer, booze

explanation.surface: Drinking good beer causes flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'responsible for' is a link phrase. The surface suggests beer-induced wind, a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A gale is a very strong wind, so a lot of wind.

clue.text: Prepared crackers before daybreak

parts.note: crackers is slang for mad
ere is an old word for before
the word day broken up gives its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Biscuits got ready before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits; it means mad. 'daybreak' looks like dawn; it is DAY broken, ADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something made ready has been prepared.

clue.text: Try repeating line from Russian author

indicators.note: repeating means the word for try is given twice

parts.note: a go is a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: Attempting again and again a line from a Russian writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was a nineteenth-century Russian writer, author of Dead Souls.
